title: Choose the visual world for the PINN flow viewer
question: The roll assigned the marbling bath. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Marbling Bath
options.lineage: Ottoman ebru and European marbled endpapers
options.thesis: Flow made visible the way it first was: pigment floating on water, carried by the network's own predicted current.
materials: floating pigment on a size bath
options.viewport: The bath fills the window and the live network drags pigment drops across it; the reference lies beside it as the pulled print on the drying rack; the verdict and its number are stamped on the rim.
options.risk: Reads decorative to scientists if pigment ever covers the measurements; error maps must stay perceptual colour maps, not pigment.

raised.raise: Every number shows its source: measured values in solid type with their STATUS.md origin, reference-derived values in hairline.
Every choice stays on screen at once (all seven scenes, all Reynolds numbers, the whole time range), the active one struck forward; no hidden dropdowns.
Each metric owns a fixed place and precision in tabular digits, so values change while the layout never moves.
Each scene owns one pigment as its spot colour, carried through its tile, its controls and its charts.
One dominant image per screen: the bath is the territory and labels ride on its rim rather than in side panels.

options.label: An Album of Fluid Motion
options.lineage: Milton Van Dyke's 1982 photographic plate book
options.thesis: Each scene is a plate in the album every fluid dynamicist owns: black plate, white tracer light, a caption naming method, reference and verdict.
options.viewport: One spread fills the window: the network's plate on the left page, the reference plate facing it, the caption and verdict set beneath both.
options.risk: The most familiar world for this audience, and close to the black-plate scientific look most runs in this category ship.

options.label: The Deep Dive
options.lineage: technical wall dives with dive-computer logs
options.thesis: The benchmarks as a descent, the predicted current carrying marine snow past each stage.
options.viewport: A vertical depth axis lists the scenes as dive stages; the current scene's flow fills the water with drifting particles; depth-gauge digits carry the verdict number.
options.case: Holds audience identification through water and drifting tracers; loses on clarity, because depth stands in for difficulty, which is not a quantity of these flows.
options.risk: Lands near the near-black-plus-one-cyan default of scientific software.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: Each model's life from training run to verdict as one custody ribbon.
options.viewport: A ribbon runs from the training budget through the diagnoses to the verdict.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the audience came to see flows, not the custody of a model.
options.kept: Every number carries its source and certainty.
options.risk: Buries the flow under its history.

options.label: Struck Cathode Gauze
options.thesis: Every option present as a ghost, the chosen one struck forward in orange.
options.viewport: Scenes and Reynolds numbers hang as unlit ghosts behind a mesh, the active one glowing.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an instrument costume the flow images would fight.
options.kept: All choices visible at once, the active one struck forward.

options.label: Nixie Laboratory Counter
options.thesis: Every metric as a bank of glowing tubes.
options.viewport: Tube banks for each verdict number above the flow.
options.case: Fuses poorly: makes the numbers the show instead of the flow.
options.kept: Fixed digit places and precision for every metric.

options.label: Mid-century Magazine Programme
options.thesis: Each scene an issue with its own spot colour and a strict two-column grid.
options.viewport: A masthead and two columns of explanation beside the flow.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an editorial world for an audience that came for a live instrument.
options.kept: One spot colour per scene, held everywhere.
options.risk: Turns the viewer into a magazine.

options.label: Polish Film Poster
options.thesis: One painted metaphor swallowing the sheet.
options.viewport: The flow as one painted metaphor with the title bent into it.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a painted metaphor would replace the measured flow.
options.kept: One dominant image per screen, secondary matter on its rim.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A ParaView-style scientific viewer, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Scene tree on the left, the viewport in the centre, a properties panel on the right.
